definition: a commander of a fleet or a navy
hook: There is no D in admiral. English added one by mistake and never took it out.
modernAnchor: Gold braid, a flagship, a fleet riding at anchor. We call him an admiral.
journey: Arabic amir meant commander, and the title amir al-bahr named the commander of the sea.
Sicilian and Crusader courts borrowed the rank, but they borrowed it in fragments, often just amir al, commander of the, with no sea attached.
Medieval scribes heard a familiar Latin word hiding inside the sound and spelled it admiral, as though it came from admirari, to wonder at.
The D is that guess, set in writing and never removed. The sea the title was built on fell out of the word entirely.
